minutes.headline: Committee tells select board it still favors demolishing the Brooks House, not selling or leasing it
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee spent most of the meeting revisiting the Brooks House, reaffirming that a majority favors demolition rather than pursuing the November town meeting charge to prepare it for sale or lease, citing parking constraints on the adjacent library and doubts about commercial viability. It also reviewed the Taylor and Burns cost estimate and warrant article language for the Town Hall/Ritter building project, planned public open houses and additional meetings ahead of spring town meeting, and approved prior minutes before adjourning.

what_happened.line: Committee reaffirmed that a majority still favors demolishing the Brooks House rather than following town meeting's November charge to prepare it for sale or lease.
Committee reviewed a construction cost estimate and warrant article language for the Town Hall/Ritter building project ahead of spring town meeting.
Finance Committee reported it voted to recommend the Town Hall/Ritter warrant article, with one dissent.
Committee limited planned open houses to the Town Hall and Ritter buildings, leaving Brooks House out of that outreach.
An additional meeting was set for April 29, alongside the previously scheduled April 21 meeting, to prepare the town meeting presentation.

why_it_matters: Whether the Brooks House is demolished or sold/leased affects parking at the adjacent library and how the town follows through on what town meeting itself voted last November.

The Town Hall/Ritter building project is headed to a warrant article at spring town meeting, so the cost estimate and the Finance Committee's recommendation are what residents will be asked to vote on.
Operating and maintenance costs for the proposed new building were raised as not yet modeled, a gap that bears on what the project costs the town after construction.
